+## #2870 - One small model for the five-axis catalog case
+
+**What was decided:** Use one closed faceted cylinder for Swarf, 5-Axis Contour, and 5-Axis Flow.
+The cylinder has a 12 mm radius and extends from X = -24 mm to X = 24 mm.
+Its original analytic generator uses 16 circumference sections and six length sections.
+The OBJ generator writes each vertex once and indexes the shared vertex list to avoid the import defect tracked in [#3298](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3298).
+The operations cut between Z = 11 mm and Z = 5 mm, with clearance at Z = 25 mm.
+Use the Tilt-head 5-axis machine and a BN-0600 ball-nose cutter with a 60 mm flute and a 6 mm shank.
+Select no holder and disable the optional Contour and Flow shank-avoidance search.
+The case was held on #3300 (no opening rotary pose).
+That fix is on main, so the case now posts with no change to any check.
+
+**Why:** One model gives all three strategies a common tilted wall and surface.
+It avoids neighboring bodies that these per-source checks do not test.
+The coarse mesh and small path set keep the case inside its 60 s catalog budget (about 11 s in debug).
+The long flute and narrow shank keep the modeled tool clear above the selected wall region.
+Generation, verification, and posting remain required steps in the script.
+The README states the limits of this modeled tool assembly and the checks.
+The Swarf passes lie along the cylinder's rulings (parallel to X) with the tool axis along the ruling.
+This is the documented law of the Swarf kernel (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/swarf.rs`), not a defect.
+The README tells the reader to expect `B90.` / `B-90.` there.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** A vertical or drafted wall for Swarf. The ruling finder (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/ruling.rs`) refuses a wall ruled along Z by design and sends it to 5-Axis Contour.
+Separate wall and cap bodies would show more geometry, but would add a neighboring body outside each operation's source.
+A finer mesh and denser paths would increase the case runtime without adding a required behavior.
+Physical machine validation and posed stock-removal simulation are outside this example's scope.
+An unrelated positioning operation or a machine without rated rotary limits would have hidden the #3300 posting defect.
+Both workarounds were dropped.
+No safety check is bypassed.
+
+**Cost to change later:** Edit the generator and script, regenerate the mesh, project, and NC program, then repeat the catalog checks.
+Additional bodies need checks that include those bodies before the example can claim assembly clearance.
+No application behavior, dependency, or safety check changes for this case.

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+# Five-axis wall and surface paths
+
+This case shows Swarf, 5-Axis Contour, and 5-Axis Flow on one original faceted cylinder.
+The three operations cut the same tilted upper facets, so you can compare how each strategy sets the tool axis.
+
+The cylinder has a 12 mm radius and extends from X = -24 mm to X = 24 mm.
+Its generator divides the circumference into 16 sections and the length into six sections.
+The closed mesh includes both end caps.
+The OBJ generator writes each vertex once and indexes the shared vertex list.
+This avoids the import defect tracked in [#3298](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3298).
+
+All three operations cut the tilted facets between Z = 11 mm and Z = 5 mm.
+They use the built-in **Tilt-head 5-axis** machine and a 15-degree lead angle.
+The clearance plane is Z = 25 mm.
+The paths show three strategies over the same model.
+They do not describe a production machining sequence.
+
+| Operation | What to inspect |
+| --- | --- |
+| Swarf wall | The passes run along the cylinder's straight rulings (parallel to X). The tool lies along the ruling, so its flank touches the wall along a line. Look for `B90.` / `B-90.` on these passes, with `A0.` or the 15-degree lead (`A15.` / `A-15.`). |
+| Contour surface | The waterline passes go around the part at constant Z. The tool axis leans from the contact normal by the lead angle, so `A` and `B` change around each ring. |
+| Flow surface | The passes follow the surface direction across the facets. The `A` and `B` words change smoothly along each pass. |
+
+In `five-axis.nc`, each operation section starts with a rapid move that states `A` and `B` before the first tilted feed.
+The post needs that opening pose because the machine states rotary rate limits.
+`G43.4` turns on tool centre point control, so the X, Y and Z words are tool-tip positions.
+
+The saved project embeds the mesh, so it opens without a source-file link.
+
+The tool starts from the BN-0600 catalog ball-nose cutter.
+The case sets its flute length to 60 mm and its shank diameter to 6 mm.
+It selects no holder.
+Contour and Flow disable their optional shank-avoidance search.
+These choices keep the example small and give the modeled cutter room above the wall.
+They do not define a physical tool assembly.
+
+`build.camscript` generates all three operations and requires `cam.verify()` to return a clean result before it saves and posts.
+The catalog tests require regeneration, a script rebuild, and an NC byte comparison.
+This case does not demonstrate posed stock-removal simulation or a run on a physical machine.
+
+To regenerate the mesh and rebuild the case, run these commands from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python3 examples/catalog/multiaxis/five-axis/model/gen_five_axis_obj.py
+cargo xtask catalog --case multiaxis/five-axis
+```
+
+To check the case, run these commands:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --check --case multiaxis/five-axis
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog catalog_multiaxis_five_axis
+```
+
+The geometry and the generator are original analytic constructions.
+They use no HSMWorks model, output, or asset.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Provenance: original faceted cylinder from analytic geometry."""
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def write_mesh(name, triangles):
+    lines = ["# Original five-axis catalog geometry, millimetres."]
+    vertices = {}
+    faces = []
+    for triangle in triangles:
+        face = []
+        for x, y, z in triangle:
+            key = tuple(round(value, 9) for value in (x, y, z))
+            if key not in vertices:
+                vertices[key] = len(vertices) + 1
+            face.append(vertices[key])
+        faces.append(face)
+    lines.extend(f"v {x:.9f} {y:.9f} {z:.9f}" for x, y, z in vertices)
+    lines.extend(f"f {a} {b} {c}" for a, b, c in faces)
+    Path(__file__).with_name(name + ".obj").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+
+def wall():
+    """Closed radius-12 cylinder with straight rulings parallel to X."""
+    def point(j, i):
+        angle = math.tau * j / 16
+        return (-24 + 48 * i / 6, 12 * math.cos(angle), 12 * math.sin(angle))
+
+    triangles = []
+    for j in range(16):
+        for i in range(6):
+            a, b = point(j, i), point((j + 1) % 16, i)
+            c, d = point((j + 1) % 16, i + 1), point(j, i + 1)
+            triangles.extend([(a, b, c), (a, c, d)])
+        triangles.extend([
+            ((24, 0, 0), point(j, 6), point((j + 1) % 16, 6)),
+            ((-24, 0, 0), point((j + 1) % 16, 0), point(j, 0)),
+        ])
+    return triangles
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    write_mesh("five-axis", wall())
